status: v2: terms added after run own_v1 (forced fits showed missing behaviors)

conventions.tree: In 'facets', an object is a parent node and a string is a leaf (the string is its meaning). A parent means 'any of its leaves'. '_doc' describes a parent.
conventions.one_word_per_behavior: Each behavior has exactly one action name. Synonyms must map to the same name (e.g. 'keep going, don't stop' -> pause_for_user_approval with modality F).
conventions.action_types: bool: done or not. int: a number with a unit (approximations become intervals). enum: exactly one value at a time, so different values exclude each other automatically.
conventions.extension: The translator may add a new leaf only under an existing parent, or a new action with a type. Each addition is logged for review.

task._doc: What the agent is doing when the rule applies (the trigger).

respond._doc: Writing a reply to the user in chat.
respond.answer_question: Answering a question or reporting a result.
respond.check_user_understanding: User restates a concept in their own words or asks 'am I understanding this right'.
respond.give_drill_answer: Model answer, drill response, or study-tracker entry.

change_files.pointed_edit: The user points at one specific item to change.
change_files.write_course_material: Writing course notes, problem sets, or cheat sheets.

task.after_merge: Right after a branch is merged to main.

artifact._doc: Which file or document the output is part of (only when medium = file).

module_notes._doc: Per-module lecture notes of a course.

situation._doc: Yes/no facts about the moment; used in conditions and 'unless'.
situation.user_confirmed: The user explicitly approved the action.
situation.user_requested: The user explicitly asked for it.
situation.only_user_can_do: The step needs something only the user can do (secrets, login, deploy approval).
situation.plan_changed: The problem or plan changed mid-task.

use_bold_topic_sentences.doc: Each subsection starts with a bold topic sentence.

body_layout.doc: Where the body text goes relative to the bold topic sentence.

response_line_count.doc: Length of the whole report in lines; ONLY when the rule states a number (e.g. 'one line').

include_filler_or_caveats.doc: Add padding: caveats, alternative framings, asides, restating, unrequested detail. (Specific content; for overall length use be_brief.)

include_full_explanation.doc: A normal explanation of the concept.

include_causal_chain.doc: context -> finding -> why it matters -> fix.

include_issue_fix_expected.doc: Issue, fix, and expected behavior after an edit.

include_edit_summary.doc: What was modified, core code, expected behavior.

be_brief.doc: Keep the whole output short (no number stated). 'concise', 'short', 'brief'.

narrate_process.doc: Narrate the work step by step (play-by-play) instead of giving the result.

offer_followup_detail.doc: Mention in one line that more detail is available, without giving it.

close_with_recommendation.doc: End a section with a one-line recommendation.

restate_when_changed.doc: Explicitly re-state the problem/plan and what changed when it changes.

lines_per_item.doc: Length of one list item / note, in lines.

state_plan_first.doc: Say the plan before acting (does not require waiting).

pause_for_user_approval.doc: Stop and wait for the user's go-ahead before continuing. ('keep going', 'run back-to-back', 'don't stop' = modality F.)

ask_user_to_choose.doc: Ask the user to pick between options. ('decide yourself' = modality F.)

show_prototype.doc: Show something runnable/visible at the end of a stage.

work_incrementally.doc: Make changes in small steps rather than many at once. (Not about stopping or asking.)

edit_beyond_target.doc: Change content beyond what the user pointed at (scope creep in an edit).

read_full_memory_file.doc: Read the linked memory file, not only its index line.

fabricate_information.doc: Make up facts, reasoning, or conclusions.

let_effort_drive_decisions.doc: Let implementation effort or complexity decide a technical choice.

verify_prerequisite_first.doc: Check that a prerequisite holds (access, state) before starting a step.

confirm_files_with_user.doc: Show the file list and get approval.

confirm_target_db.doc: Confirm which database with the user.

not_seeded_yet: Codebase-specific rules (e.g. CAST(... AS NUMERIC) in CASE...WHEN, edit<X>Repository status transitions) are left for controlled extension; expect them under task.change_files.write_code with new actions.
A 'project' facet is omitted: pairs are only checked within one session, where the project is fixed.
